candidacy.title: Candidacy Committee
candidacy.subtitle: Guiding aspiring CRCA Ministers of the Word from initial discernment through theological study at RTC, mentoring, supervised vicariate, and Classis examination.
intro: If you are considering ordained pastoral ministry in the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia, we encourage you to connect with the Candidacy Committee before beginning your theological studies.

The CRCA encourages ministry candidates to study through the Reformed Theological College (RTC) and then complete a supervised one-year vicariate (internship alongside an experienced senior minister). The Candidacy Committee oversees this journey through a State Representative in every Classis alongside a national Executive based in Geelong, Victoria.

tracks.title: 4-Year Study at RTC (Preferred Option)
tracks.description: Full four-year theological formation at the Reformed Theological College in preparation for pastoral ministry and CRCA vicariate.

tracks.title: Task3 Pathway (2 Years Church-Based + 2 Years RTC)
tracks.description: Combines two years of hands-on ministry training in a local CRCA congregation with two years of study at RTC.

tracks.title: Prior Theological Degree + 1 Year at RTC
tracks.description: Designed for candidates who have completed theological training at another recognised college and undertake a consolidating year at RTC.

tracks.title: Alternative College + Required RTC Units
tracks.description: For students studying at another accredited theological institution who complete required Reformed and CRCA-specific units at RTC.

steps.title: Initial Contact
steps.description: Speak first with your local minister, then contact your State/Classis Representative (via your Classis Clerk) or the National Chair. Write to the Candidacy Committee outlining your desire and motives for entering ordained ministry in the CRCA.

steps.title: Letter of Recommendation
steps.description: The committee requests a reference from your home Church Council assessing Christian character (1 Timothy 3) and how your gifts have been demonstrated in local church ministry.

steps.title: Psychological Profiling & Screening
steps.description: Candidates complete psychological profiling along with a Working With Children Check (or state equivalent) and a National Police Check.

steps.title: Approved Study Program
steps.description: The Candidacy Committee consults with RTC to map out and approve your study requirements along one of the four recognised ordination tracks.

steps.title: Candidacy Approval
steps.description: Once approved as a Ministry Candidate, the committee notifies you, your local Church Council, and RTC — making you eligible for RTC student subsidies and denominational candidate funding.

steps.title: Annual Reviews
steps.description: Each year during study, the committee meets with you (alongside an annual report from RTC) to review spiritual growth, personal development, academic progress, family and church life, and financial or special needs.

steps.title: Dedicated Mentoring
steps.description: You are paired with an assigned mentor who supports you throughout your training and walks with you through any areas highlighted during recommendations, profiling, or faculty reviews.

steps.title: Final Approval for Vicariate
steps.description: Upon finishing your degree, the committee — in close consultation with RTC faculty and your mentor(s) — assesses readiness to enter a supervised vicariate (with a right of appeal to your sending Church Council if withheld).

steps.title: One-Year Supervised Vicariate
steps.description: Working with CRCA congregations, the committee arranges your placement with a supervising minister and maintains regular check-ins with both you and your supervisor throughout the year.

steps.title: Preliminary Examination (Eligibility for Call)
steps.description: Near the end of your vicariate, you apply through the host Church Council for a Preliminary Examination at your local Classis. Upon passing, Classis declares you eligible to be called as a Minister of the Word and Sacraments.

steps.title: Final Examination & Ordination
steps.description: Upon accepting a formal call from a local congregation, you submit to a Final Examination before the calling Classis (Church Order Article 10) in accordance with the Rules for the Final Examination, and are then ordained and installed as a Minister of the Word and Sacraments.

shiftCoaching.title: Shift Coaching
shiftCoaching.subtitle: Intentional peer, elder, and ministry coaching helping CRCA pastors and Church Councils grow in love, disciple-making, leadership multiplication, outreach, and lifelong learning.
shiftCoaching.openingVerse: “I urge you to live a life worthy of the calling you have received.” (Ephesians 4:1)
shiftCoaching.proverbVerse: “As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.” (Proverbs 27:17)
intro: Shift is all about movement — with the help of one another and the power of God to reach our broken places and live lives worthy of our calling as churches and leaders. Leadership development begins by trusting the people God uses to grow us, because we cannot lead others where we have not first walked ourselves.

Every CRCA pastor is encouraged to establish an intentional coaching relationship — whether with a ministerial peer, an elder, a wise and mature member of the congregation, or a professional coach — where the five rhythm questions below (rated on a scale of 1–10) are discussed regularly. Church Councils are also encouraged to actively review and support the ongoing development of their pastor(s).
shiftCoaching.pdpNote: Need the Shift Professional Development Process guide for a Church Council or Classis review? Request a copy directly from CRCA Ministry Development via admin@crca.org.au.

rhythms.title: Love One Another
questions: How would you rate your own passion and love for God and His people? What do you need to do to move that one more step toward 10?
How visible to those outside the church is the love your members have for one another? What could be done to move that one more step toward 10?

resources.title: 5 Things to Pray for Your Church
resources.author: Rachel Jones

resources.title: The 10-Second Rule: Following Jesus Made Simple
resources.author: Clare de Graaf

rhythms.title: Discipleship
questions: What is your own “discipleship temperature”? What are you personally doing to grow disciples in your church? What could you do to move that one more step toward 10?

How would you rate the culture of “growing disciples” across the congregation (among members, not just from the pastor)? What initiatives are building that culture, and what moves it one step closer to 10?

rhythms.title: Multiplying Leadership
questions: How would you rate yourself in training and multiplying leaders (coaching, praying for, and resourcing emerging leaders)? What do you need to do to move one step toward 10?
How are existing ministry leaders going at raising up new leaders? What is the biggest barrier holding your church back, and what is your next step toward 10?

resources.title: Leadership Essentials: Shaping Vision, Multiplying Influence, Defining Character
resources.author: Greg Ogden & Daniel Meyer

resources.title: Passing the Baton: A Handbook for Ministry Apprenticeship
resources.author: Colin Marshall

rhythms.title: Reaching the Lost
questions: How would you rate your own personal “outreach temperature”? What would you need to do to move one step closer to 10?
How would you rate the “outreach temperature” of your congregation? Where can your church intentionally leverage its time, hospitality, ministries, and love toward neighbours still far from God?

rhythms.title: Professional Development
rhythms.contextNote: Designed to be asked regularly at Church Council / Session meetings, Classis meetings, and during mutual Church Visitation:
questions: What is your Church Council / Session doing to ensure your minister has a plan for ongoing personal and professional learning — and what time, finances, or coaching are being provided to support it?
What are you doing as a minister for your personal and professional growth, what helps fulfil your development plan, and what learning could encourage your colleagues across Classis?

local-church-outreach-training.title: Local Church Outreach Training
local-church-outreach-training.subtitle: Organic Outreach — equipping everyday church members across Australia to share the good news of Jesus naturally.
local-church-outreach-training.overviewHeading: Weaving evangelism into the DNA of everyday church life
paragraphs: Most churches agree that evangelism matters. As the CRCA declares, reaching the lost is central to our calling: we are a church reforming to reach the lost for Christ. Yet many congregations find it hard to move beyond maintaining the status quo.

Many Christians genuinely want to share their faith, but hesitate because they do not want gospel conversations to feel awkward, scripted, or unnatural — either for themselves or for the friends and neighbours God has placed around them.

Jesus tells His followers that they are the light of the world and the salt of the earth — called to let God’s grace shine in families, workplaces, and neighbourhoods. Through Australian cohorts, ongoing coaching, and a partnership with Organic Outreach International, CRCA Ministry Development walks alongside local churches to help everyday members share Christ naturally.
local-church-outreach-training.calloutTitle: Join an Australian Organic Outreach Cohort
local-church-outreach-training.calloutBody: Ministry Development helps CRCA congregations initiate Organic Outreach locally, connect into Australian coaching cohorts, and receive ongoing implementation support.
local-church-outreach-training.highlightsHeading: How CRCA Ministry Development helps your church
highlights: Australian Organic Outreach coaching cohorts for pastors, elders, and outreach teams.
Practical training that moves evangelism from high-pressure guilt to natural everyday relationships.
Access to Organic Outreach International conference recordings, interviews, and free church tools.
Ongoing coaching tailored to your congregation’s local neighbourhood context.

missional-explorations.title: Missional Explorations
missional-explorations.subtitle: A stepping-stone between everyday local outreach and formal church planting — backed by up to $2,500 in matching CPT seed funding.
missional-explorations.overviewHeading: Standing in the gap between outreach and church planting
paragraphs: Missional Explorations are designed to help local congregations test and nurture new missional contexts that might one day grow into future church plants. Under the oversight of a local Session, a Missional Exploration creates space for an outreach initiative to take on a life of its own.

Formal church planting can often feel like a bridge too far. Missional Explorations stand intentionally in that gap — supporting local teams to test new gospel work whether or not a standalone church plant eventually emerges, confident that Christ is proclaimed and real communities are reached.
These initiatives can take shape in natural places of shared community life: through a local sporting club, around a playgroup, within a school community, or among neighbours in a growing suburb.
missional-explorations.calloutTitle: Up to $2,500 Matching Seed Grants Available
missional-explorations.calloutBody: The Church Planting Taskforce (CPT) matches funding dollar-for-dollar up to $2,500 alongside your local congregation to resource emerging missional teams.
missional-explorations.highlightsHeading: What Missional Explorations seed grants can fund
highlights: Core-team training and coaching
Practical outreach equipment purchases
Community venue hire and hospitality
Printed promotional materials and local invitations
Exploratory gatherings around sporting clubs, playgroups, school communities, or new estates

church-planting-taskforce.title: Church Planting Taskforce (CPT)
church-planting-taskforce.subtitle: Encouraging, researching, and resourcing CRCA congregations to plant and revitalise Reformed churches across Australia.
church-planting-taskforce.overviewHeading: Multiplying healthy gospel churches across Australia
paragraphs: The Church Planting Taskforce (CPT) serves the CRCA nationally by encouraging local congregations and Classes in the joyful work of planting new churches and revitalising existing gospel witness across Australia.

Alongside research and strategic guidance, the CPT partners directly with congregations through Missional Explorations matching seed grants (up to $2,500) to bridge everyday local outreach and new church plants.
church-planting-taskforce.calloutTitle: Looking for seed funding to test a new ministry context?
church-planting-taskforce.calloutBody: Explore our Missional Explorations grant pathway — matching up to $2,500 with local churches to resource core teams, venue hire, and outreach.
church-planting-taskforce.highlightsHeading: Key areas of CPT research and encouragement
highlights: Evaluating the effectiveness of multiplying congregations across Australia
Developing models of both church reinvigoration and new church planting
Strengthening the financial sustainability and development of congregations
Tracking base numbers and goal numbers across our church-planting mission
Mapping geographical and sociological communities where the CRCA is not yet reaching people
Identifying where congregations can pursue the most effective gospel outreach

pdfs.description: Apply for matching seed grants up to $2,500 administered by the CPT.

ecumenical-relations.title: Committee of Ecumenical Relations
ecumenical-relations.subtitle: Fostering confessional unity, mission cooperation, and sister-church fellowship with Reformed denominations across Australia and around the globe.
ecumenical-relations.overviewHeading: Pursuing gospel unity across the global Reformed family
paragraphs: Under Church Order Article 52 and Synodical mandate, the CRCA maintains rich, fruitful relationships with sister Reformed and Presbyterian churches both within Australia and internationally.

The synodical Committee of Ecumenical Relations (CER) currently comprises three members located across Australia, meeting regularly online throughout the year to cultivate mutual encouragement, confessional integrity, and shared participation in international Reformed assemblies.
ecumenical-relations.calloutBody: The CRCA is an active member of the ICRC, collaborating with confessional Reformed churches around the world in doctrine, mission, and diaconal mercy.
highlights: Facilitate contact with Reformed and Presbyterian churches toward mutually beneficial ecumenical fellowship.
Participate in ecumenical organisations where the CRCA holds membership in accordance with Church Order and Synod decisions.
Develop relationships grounded in Reformed confessions, polity, and liturgy, bilateral agreements, and shared ICRC membership.
Pursue mutual understanding, mission and diaconal cooperation, proclamation of Christ’s Kingdom, and visible unity (Church Order Art. 52).
Facilitate ecumenical relationships in accordance with Synodical decisions regarding Churches in Ecclesiastical Fellowship (CEF).
Keep CRCA congregations informed of developments within Churches in Ecclesiastical Fellowship through study and contact.
Advise Synod on the fruitfulness of established relationships, new CEF candidates, fellowship levels, and international affiliations.
